note: The Republic of China on Taiwan still claims to be the government of all China and plans to return to the mainland.
Beijing regards Taiwan as a rebel province; the Taiwan Strait crises of 1954 and 1958 nearly led to war.
Both Korean states claim the whole peninsula; the 1953 armistice line divides them.

Bonn claims to speak for all Germans and refuses to recognise the East German state (the Hallstein Doctrine).
Hanoi seeks to reunify Vietnam under its rule; the 1956 elections promised at Geneva never took place.
Saigon also claims to be the legitimate government of all Vietnam.
West New Guinea: under the August 1962 New York Agreement the Dutch hand it to a UN authority now, and to Indonesia in May 1963.
China rejects the McMahon Line and holds Aksai Chin; border clashes are escalating toward open war.
Pakistan disputes Indian rule in Kashmir and calls for the plebiscite promised by the UN in 1948.
India claims all of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir.
Argentina presses its claim to the Islas Malvinas at the UN.
Franco's Spain is reviving its claim to Gibraltar before the UN decolonisation committee.
Guatemala claims British Honduras as its own territory.

_regions: Natural Earth shuffles Guyana's region names, so these are the map's labels, not the real regions. West of the Essequibo the map's Barima-Waini, Pomeroon-Supenaam (really Cuyuni-Mazaruni), Potaro-Siparuni and Upper Demerara-Berbice (really Upper Takutu-Upper Essequibo, ~3/4 west of the river) are claimed. Its Cuyuni-Mazaruni (really Pomeroon-Supenaam merged with Demerara and Georgetown) and Upper Takutu-Upper Essequibo (really Upper Demerara-Berbice) lie mostly east of the river and are left out.
note: In 1962 Venezuela declared the 1899 award over British Guiana's border null and void.
Morocco claims Spanish Sahara as part of a Greater Morocco.
Morocco refuses to recognise Mauritania's independence and claims it as Moroccan land.
Qasim's Iraq claims Kuwait as a lost province; British and Arab League troops deterred an invasion in 1961.
The Ogaden: Somalia seeks to unite all Somali-inhabited lands.
The Northern Frontier District of Kenya, mostly Somali, wants to join Somalia.
Syria has never accepted the 1939 transfer of the Sanjak of Alexandretta to Turkey.
Okinawa remains under American administration; Japan keeps residual sovereignty and seeks its return.
